summary: This diff adds thin, auth-gated PROJEXA proxy routes (GET /api/scope/[id], POST /api/scope/[id]/revisions, GET /api/scope/[id]/compare) that mirror the existing /api/scope/route.ts pattern exactly (requireAuth() first, org-scoped callVeridian(), VeridianApiError passthrough, encodeURIComponent on all path/query interpolation, no injection surface), plus a ScopeClient.tsx extension (variation column, New Revision dialog with a 409-driven override flow, Compare dialog) that is well-tested (6 new route tests covering the 401 path and the 409-scope-reduction passthrough specifically) and type-checks clean (verified tsc --noEmit locally, no errors). It is purely additive (new files + non-breaking UI extension), touches no migrations/schema/auth internals/.github/workflows, and does not modify computeHierarchicalAmount or any cron/timer file, matching tier1 classification. The real functional risk is a cross-repo ordering dependency: these routes call VERIDIAN endpoints (GET /scope/[id], POST /scope/[id]/revisions, GET /scope/[id]/compare) that per the PROGRESS.md were added in compliance-tracker PR #605, which is explicitly still open/unmerged -- until that PR merges, the New Revision and Compare actions will fail (gracefully, via caught fetch errors and toasts, not a crash) in production. A secondary, pre-existing (not introduced here) gap is that revision creation has no requireRole() gate the way budgets/change-orders do, mirroring the same gap already present in the sibling POST /api/scope endpoint.
issues: Cross-repo merge ordering: this PR's New-Revision/Compare features depend on compliance-tracker PR #605 (VERIDIAN's GET /scope/[id], POST /scope/[id]/revisions, GET /scope/[id]/compare endpoints), which is explicitly not yet merged -- these actions will 502/error in production until that PR lands. Degrades gracefully (caught + toast, no crash) but sequence the merges so #605 lands first or the feature ships visibly broken.

No requireRole() gate on POST /api/scope/[id]/revisions -- any authenticated org member can create a scope revision with real cost/variation impact, unlike PM_OR_ABOVE-gated budgets/change-orders. This mirrors a pre-existing gap in POST /api/scope (BOQ creation itself is also ungated), so it is not a regression introduced by this diff, but worth a follow-up given revisions carry real variation cost.
Minor: ScopeClient.load() issues one /compare fetch per existing revision (N+1) to populate the variation column -- fine at current scale, could get slow on projects with many revisions.
